new_findings_today.title: Khonoma SOS contains a text-typed `phone` field (`"Contact via Kohima tourism office"`) — schema violation
new_findings_today.detail: /en/destination/khonoma embeds an SOS contact whose `phone` field is the free-text string `Contact via Kohima tourism office` rather than a phone-formatted value or null. This is structurally different from yesterday's NEW-2026-05-10-001 Uttarkashi `+91-94120-XXXXX` placeholder (which masqueraded as a real number) — it's an honest description, but the consuming UI assumes `phone` is dialable (renders as `tel:` link or fails to render). Per CLAUDE.md "All data must be real and verifiable... Honest scarcity (`[]`) preferred over fabrication" — a text-typed phone is neither: it's a fallback. The other 3 Khonoma phones (0370-2243011, 0370-2290142, 112) are valid Indian formats. Across the 10-destination sample, this is the only invalid-format phone (1/14 = 7%). Note: 3 destinations (candolim, mysore, ajanta-caves) returned 0 phones — these are honest-scarcity nulls, not fabrications.
new_findings_today.evidence: section-E-sos.csv — khonoma row: 4 phones extracted, 1 invalid_format = `Contact via Kohima tourism office`. Source HTML context (RSC payload, double-escaped): `\"phone\":\"Contact via Kohima tourism office\"`.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Either (a) replace the text string with the actual Kohima tourism office number (0370-2243011 already in the same Khonoma SOS array, so this row is redundant), or (b) drop the contact row and let scarcity stand (preferred). Then sweep the corpus: `grep -roE '\\?"phone\\?":\s*\\?"[^0-9+\\"]' data/sos/ supabase/seed*.sql` to find any other text-typed phone fields.
